Accor's largest shareholder wants a change at the top. Parvus Asset Management, a London-based activist fund that holds about 14% of the group, is calling for Sébastien Bazin to step down as Chairman and CEO. The Financial Times first reported the move, and Reuters, relayed by Boursorama, and Hedgeweek followed on 20 November 2026.

## What Parvus is asking for

The fund is asking for "urgent change" at the head of the group. Its criticism, as reported by Hedgeweek, is twofold: a strategy it finds hard to read, and capital it says is allocated inconsistently.

The trigger is recent. On 17 November, Accor signed a memorandum to buy the 44.3% of Ennismore it does not yet own, for about €1.6 billion, in tranches running to January 2028. Ennismore is the lifestyle platform behind brands such as The Hoxton, Mama Shelter and Paris Society. Parvus argues that a leadership already preparing its exit should not commit to a cheque of that size.

If the board does not act, the fund says it could push for changes to the board and to management at the next annual general meeting.

## A succession already under way

Sébastien Bazin has led Accor since 2013. He had already said he would hand over by 2028, and a search for his successor is under way. Accor's official response to Parvus had not been published in the sources we read.

## The signal

A succession that was meant to be orderly is now on a clock. Whoever takes over will inherit the Ennismore deal and a shareholder watching every euro of capital spending. For the wider industry, it is a reminder that the large hotel groups are now judged as much on capital allocation as on brands and openings.
summary: Activist fund Parvus, with about 14% of Accor, is calling for Chairman and CEO Sébastien Bazin to step down, days after the group's €1.6bn deal to buy out its partners in Ennismore.
title: Accor's largest shareholder wants Sébastien Bazin out
why: A succession that was meant to be calm is now on a clock.
